tasks.short: Negotiate collective agreements within an approved mandate and secure valid agreement.

steps.what: Assemble proposals, cost scenarios and outstanding issues into a bargaining pack.
Agree negotiating limits, concessions and escalation points.
Bargain with employee representatives and test concessions within the mandate.
Write the session record and consolidate tentative terms.

loop.input: Written negotiation notes and expressly recorded tentative terms.
loop.output: Source-linked session record and settlement draft with unresolved wording marked.
loop.check: Specialist checks every commitment against notes; conflicting accounts remain unresolved.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing or disputed terms return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes need synthesis; templates alone cannot distinguish discussion from agreement.

steps.what: Check settlement wording against applicable law and existing agreements.
Approve settlement terms or return outstanding issues to negotiation.
Complete required ratification, signatures and agreement filing.

tasks.design: A controlled pack generator assembles approved material from the {DOCS}, {CLM} and {SPREADSHEET}; a bounded drafting loop prepares session records from written notes. Configure the {WORKFLOW} and {ESIGN} for settlement approvals and signatures, while people retain bargaining, legal review and ratification.
tasks.previous_blocker: The central work depends on trust, mandates and concessions. Supporting documents have separate owners and changing versions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval and signature features handle routing. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building pack assembly and document checks; bounded drafting can reduce note preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing terms remains slow and political. Sector agreements, national rules and representative ratification can constrain local authority.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, preserve trust and judge when a concession creates a workable agreement.

ambition.what: Joint implementation readiness review before an agreement takes effect.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into assembling packs and recording meetings; bargaining remains most of the work. The specialist can coordinate implementation readiness, but gains no additional settlement authority.

reach.task: Translate a settlement into an implementation plan.
reach.learn: Approval delegations, operational dependencies and how to assign accountable implementation owners.

evidence.claim: Pack assembly, approval routing and signature tracking are established automation patterns; bargaining remains human.
Generated documents need source checks; the digest documents a report containing nonexistent references.
Dutch works council consent rights cover specified employee-data and monitoring arrangements; other countries require national assessment.

assumptions: The employer participates directly in bargaining; where sector bodies negotiate, this task becomes local input and implementation.
Today's document, meeting and spreadsheet mix is an estimate informed by the supplied priors.
Proposal drafting and resolution design are counted in their separate tasks; this task consumes those outputs.
Build ranges cover the supporting tools, not negotiation duration. Consultation may add elapsed time.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements apply; national rules determine representation, consultation and agreement formalities.
unknowns: Who holds negotiating and signing authority?
Which ratification procedures and national rules apply?
Are agreement records in the {CLM}, the {DOCS}, or both?
Which employee or union data may be accessed, and under what lawful basis and safeguards?
research_questions: Which existing approval and signature features can support the settlement process?
Can pack generation reliably detect outdated proposal versions in a representative document sample?
new_work: Check generated session records against written notes.
Maintain mandate templates, approval routes and version rules.
Handle disputed notes, failed signatures and incomplete ratification.
Maintain access restrictions, retention settings and integration checks.

tasks.short: Investigate union complaints, assess their merits and communicate a reasoned position.

steps.what: Register the complaint, acknowledge receipt and identify procedural deadlines.
Collect relevant employment records, agreements and correspondence.
Interview the complainant, manager and relevant witnesses.
Build a chronology and map allegations to evidence and agreement clauses.

loop.input: Access-approved evidence bundle, written interview notes and current agreement.
loop.output: Chronology and allegation-to-evidence matrix with source locations and contradictions.
loop.check: Validate source locations and dates; specialist checks completeness and disputed accounts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unreadable or contradictory material enters an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Accounts and allegations appear in varied free text rather than consistent fields.

steps.what: Assess merits, procedural fairness and whether legal advice or further investigation is needed.
Draft the reasoned response and proposed next steps.

loop.input: Human case assessment, approved next steps and response template.
loop.output: Response draft explaining the assessment and procedural next steps.
loop.check: Match every finding to the approved assessment; flag unsupported legal statements.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing rationale returns to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Individual complaints require a tailored explanation beyond template fields.

steps.what: Approve and send the response through the agreed confidential channel.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted case queue in the {HELPDESK} and retrieve explicitly selected records from the {HCM}, {DOCS} and {EMAIL}. Bounded loops prepare a source-linked chronology and response draft; the specialist conducts interviews, determines the assessment and approves each external response.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence crosses restricted records and personal correspondence. Credibility, conflicting accounts and legal interpretation resist fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Case permissions, deadline rules and scoped retrieval can handle administration. Bounded extraction can organise free text without deciding complaint validity.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence may be incomplete, sensitive or contested. Union membership can be special-category data, and disclosure must protect other people's information.
tasks.human_edge: Hear people fairly, test competing accounts and make a defensible assessment without reducing credibility to a score.
tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time reconstructing files and more time on interviews and disputed facts. Case decision rights stay the same; aggregate findings can support recommendations for procedural improvements.

reach.task: Identify discrimination concerns that require a separate investigation route.
reach.learn: Referral thresholds, evidence preservation and protections against retaliation.

evidence.claim: Restricted case records, deadline tracking and evidence organisation are feasible supporting tools; the digest provides no direct labor-relations deployment case.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
Dutch consultation and consent requirements can apply to employee-data arrangements; national rules elsewhere need separate assessment.

assumptions: A restricted case queue exists in the {HELPDESK}; otherwise configure an equivalent restricted record in the {WORKFLOW}.
Retrieval uses a human-selected case scope rather than searching all employee communications.
The tool produces no credibility score, employee ranking or automated complaint decision.
Time shares are estimates; interviews and judgment remain substantial despite document automation.
Access work includes GDPR lawful-basis and special-category conditions, retention, EU AI Act intended-use assessment, and applicable national consultation.
unknowns: Which grievance deadlines and escalation procedures apply?
Which records may investigators access and disclose?
Who must approve responses in serious or legally contested cases?
Which consultation, privacy assessment and employee-information steps are required?
research_questions: Does the existing case system enforce case-specific access and disclosure controls?
Can extraction preserve contradictory accounts and identify missing evidence on representative closed cases?
new_work: Verify chronology entries, evidence links and omitted material.
Handle missing records and access exceptions.
Maintain procedure deadlines, response templates and retention rules.
Review access logs and prevent identifiable small-group reporting.

tasks.short: Develop and test resolution options for collective bargaining and labor negotiations.

steps.what: Summarise disputed issues, stated interests and constraints.

loop.input: Issue register, approved session records, relevant case assessment and current agreement.
loop.output: Resolution brief separating stated interests, binding constraints and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Cite each constraint and stated interest; specialist checks scope and inferred claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unsupported interests become questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Issues and constraints are expressed across varied narrative records.

steps.what: Calculate cost and workforce coverage for candidate concessions.
Construct alternative resolution packages and explain their trade-offs.

loop.input: Validated resolution brief, calculated scenarios and approved clause library.
loop.output: Up to three resolution packages with trade-offs, assumptions and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check numeric references against scenarios and clauses against their sources; specialist assesses realism.
loop.stop: Three packages and one revision maximum; infeasible options return for human redesign.
loop.why_not_simpler: Combining concessions into understandable packages requires contextual drafting.

steps.what: Assess fairness, legal exposure, precedent and likely acceptability.
Test a nonbinding resolution with employee representatives within existing authority.
Approve the resolution package and any revised negotiating limits.

tasks.design: A deterministic calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} uses scoped extracts from the {HCM} and {PAYROLL} to generate reproducible cost scenarios. Bounded loops turn approved records in the {DOCS} into briefs and option drafts, while people assess fairness, test acceptability and approve mandates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costing and narrative proposals are maintained separately. Resolution quality depends on context, precedent and what representatives can accept.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable calculation rules can connect packages to current workforce assumptions. Bounded drafting can express alternatives without giving a model negotiating authority.
tasks.still_hard: National rules, knock-on effects and uncertain workforce assumptions complicate costing. A financially feasible package may still be unacceptable or unfair.
tasks.human_edge: Find a concession that addresses the underlying concern and preserves a durable working relationship.

ambition.what: Reassess affordability after each material change to a bargaining package.

tasks.altitude: The specialist can compare packages during preparation instead of waiting for repeated manual costing. Settlement and mandate approval stay with existing decision makers.

reach.task: Evaluate the distribution and recurring cost of a proposed pay settlement.
reach.learn: Pay structures, employer costs, workforce assumptions and how to explain distributional effects.

evidence.claim: Formula-based scenario costing and template-based option packs are feasible; their labor-negotiation benefit is an estimate.
Source validation matters for generated recommendations; a documented report case included nonexistent references.

assumptions: The calculator models package costs and coverage; it does not recommend individual employment decisions.
Early discussions are nonbinding and covered by an existing mandate.
Approved resolutions feed proposal drafting; formal bargaining is counted separately.
A shared calculator and source library can serve the other bargaining tasks, so build ranges are not additive.
Access and rollout include GDPR controls, EU AI Act intended-use assessment and consultation under applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which pay components and employer costs must the calculator include?
How current and complete are the workforce and pay extracts?
Who validates costing assumptions and exceptional pay arrangements?
What may be shared with employee representatives before formal approval?
research_questions: Can existing payroll simulation or reporting features replace a custom calculator?
Which package types need separate calculation rules rather than narrative assumptions?
new_work: Reconcile scenario totals to approved pay baselines.
Check option drafts for invented commitments and misleading trade-offs.
Update clause sources and record why options were rejected.

tasks.short: Draft bargaining proposals and counterproposals from approved terms.

steps.what: Select the authoritative agreement, approved resolution and drafting instructions.
Write proposed clauses and counterproposal wording.

loop.input: Version-locked drafting pack, approved clause library and proposal template.
loop.output: Clause draft with a source map and unresolved choices marked.
loop.check: Compare every commitment to approved instructions; reuse approved wording verbatim where applicable.
loop.stop: One draft and two targeted revisions; unresolved intent goes back to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing clauses can be assembled deterministically, but novel counterproposal wording needs contextual drafting.

steps.what: Compare versions and check dates, amounts, definitions and cross-references.
Review legal meaning, enforceability and unintended changes.
Approve the proposal for release against the negotiating mandate.
Send the approved version and record its release.

tasks.design: A generator assembles approved clauses and instructions from the {CLM} and {DOCS}, using a bounded drafting loop only for new wording. Deterministic comparison checks produce a change report, and the {WORKFLOW} releases the approved version through the {EMAIL} after recipient confirmation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approved intentions are expressed in narrative instructions, while clause dependencies and version control require careful manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Document assembly, comparison and controlled release are established techniques. Bounded drafting can handle novel wording while retaining source maps and human legal review.
tasks.still_hard: A small wording change can alter obligations across several clauses. Legal interpretation, multilingual equivalence and missing negotiating intent remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Translate negotiated intent into precise obligations and recognise wording that creates an unintended concession.

ambition.what: Clause-level implementation impact note for each proposed agreement change.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time producing first drafts and comparisons, and more time checking intent and implementation consequences. Authority to approve or release proposals does not expand automatically.

reach.task: Translate changed agreement clauses into employee guidance and operating procedures.
reach.learn: Clause interpretation, effective-date transitions and clear explanations of employee entitlements.

evidence.claim: Clause assembly, document comparison and controlled release can use deterministic technology; contextual drafting needs review.
The digest documents fabricated references in a generated report, supporting source checks before external release.

assumptions: The task starts with approved negotiating intent; choosing concessions is counted in resolution design and bargaining.
The proposed automation prepares text and checks structure; it does not certify legal validity.
Time shares give drafting more weight than meetings because the task boundary excludes formal negotiation.
Source selection and legal review may remain substantial even when first-draft production is faster.
Access work covers confidential material, GDPR requirements where personal data appears, EU AI Act intended use and applicable national consultation.
unknowns: Is there a maintained clause library with authoritative versions?
Which languages and agreement formats are required?
Who approves wording and who may release it?
Can existing document tools produce reliable comparisons and immutable release records?
research_questions: Which recurring proposals can be generated entirely from approved clauses and structured fields?
Can checks detect changed amounts, broken references and unintended omissions in representative historical drafts?
new_work: Maintain approved clauses, templates and their effective dates.
Review novel wording and unresolved intent.
Investigate failed comparison checks and clause dependencies.
Maintain release permissions, recipient lists and source-version records.

role.altitude: The week shifts from collecting records and producing documents toward investigation, bargaining and implementation planning. Decision rights over employee outcomes, concessions and agreement approval remain with authorised people.
reach: Support compensation colleagues with reproducible settlement scenarios.
Help HR operations translate agreement changes into procedures.
Coordinate fair-investigation referrals with equal opportunity colleagues.
skills_to_grow: Define and validate deterministic costing rules.
Check source-linked drafts and evidence completeness.
Manage sensitive case access, retention and disclosure.
Translate agreement wording into operational requirements.
Evaluate tool performance without scoring employee credibility.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a continuous agreement implementation service that connects negotiated terms, cost assumptions, employee guidance and unresolved operational issues.
